title: Health and Happiness in the New Urban Agenda: The Central Role of Public Space
review_question: To examine the relationship between public spaces, health, and happiness—and human well-being more broadly—as established in the New Urban Agenda, and to explore how these quality of life aspirations can be translated into measurable targets, tools, and strategies to achieve desired outcomes.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Focuses on the New Urban Agenda (NUA) and related theoretical and empirical research connecting public space to human health, well-being, and happiness.

synthesis_conclusions: The New Urban Agenda and advancements in measuring well-being, health, and happiness represent a historic landmark achievement.
For further progress, clear connections between theory, goals, measurements, and outcomes are essential.
Policy support, alignment at multiple scales, and the development of new evidence and tools are required, involving experts, community-led initiatives, and stakeholders.
The paper successfully traced connections for health and happiness related to public space, and similar connections should be traced for other New Urban Agenda goals.
evidence_gaps: An urgent need exists to translate quality of life aspirations contained in the New Urban Agenda into measurable targets, tools, and strategies.
The proposed 'proto-indicators' require further development to be useful for guiding policy and practice.
There is a need for tools and strategies to implement interventions towards desired improvements.
Further development of theory and research is needed to sufficiently ground practice.
limitations: The proposed indicators are 'proto-indicators' and require further development.
Measurement alone is insufficient; tools and strategies are needed for intervention.
The theoretical framework needs to be further developed and grounded in practice.
The process of tracing connections between theory, goals, measurements, and outcomes is only beginning and is a much longer process.

paper_metadata.crossref_title: Health and Happiness in the New Urban Agenda: The Central Role of Public Space
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: The New Urban Agenda—the global urbanization framework agreement adopted by acclamation by all 193 countries of the United Nations—contains no fewer than eight paragraphs on the importance of public space, three of which outline its role in achieving “human health and well-being”, “attractive and liveable cities”, and “physical and mental health”. However, there is an urgent need to translate these and other quality of life aspirations contained in this landmark document into measurable targets, tools, and strategies to achieve outcomes. This paper examines the core theories that connect health and well-being to public space as reflected in the document, surveying some of the most relevant research in the field. It then analyzes the document text to identify a number of potentially useful indicators. Finally, it proposes a framework for data gathering, assessment, and iterative progress in achieving the stated goals, concluding with an overview of emerging research and practice, and proposed next steps.
